subject: Urgent: production throttling after traffic ramp — suspected quota/burst policy
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@banked.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:15-07:00
Subject: Production spike -> 429s and latency spike

Hi Monica / Laura,

Quick note from our ops team — after a scheduled traffic ramp this morning our production app started getting a large number of 429s and median generation latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s. We saw a surge around 09:05 PDT that coincides with a campaign rollout. Attached are the request traces and the throttling logs (banked_throttle_logs.zip).

Top-level impact: customer-facing errors for 4% of requests, elevated p95 token latency affecting UI responsiveness. We need an immediate mitigation path — can you confirm whether this looks like quota/burst config enforcement or an internal capacity choke?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
Banked Inc.

Attachments: banked_throttle_logs.zip (log archive), screenshot-429.png (screenshot)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@banked.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:28:03-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike -> 429s and latency spike

Thanks for the quick ping, Aisha. We're on it. Initial triage notes below:

- Dylan is looking at live throttling metrics and token bucket exhaustion events.
- Laura is pulling the customer-specific quota and burst config; that will tell us whether a policy kicked in.
- I see a partial correlation between the 09:05 ramp and a burst limit on the routing policy for your account — we will confirm.

Immediate mitigation we can try within 20–30 minutes: temporarily increase the account burst allowance and route a portion of traffic to a higher-capacity serving pool while we validate the behavior. That will require a config patch (low-risk) and a restart of the routing agent on two nodes.

Can you hold the campaign dampening for ~45 minutes while we test? If you need full rollback instructions, we can do that too.

I'll update in 15 minutes with evidence from the rate limiter logs.

- Monica
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T10:05:21-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike -> 429s and latency spike

Monica / team — quick logging dump: the token-bucket for the Banked account hit depletion on three routing workers at 09:04:57, 09:05:03, 09:05:09. KV cache hit rate was steady; CPU/mem are normal. This looks like a misaligned burst policy combined with our short-window rate enforcement.

Attached a small config diff that would raise burst window from 5s -> 20s for the account and add a temporary override to increase capacity by 30% for the next hour (config-diff.patch). Applying it to two routing nodes is non-disruptive — no model reload needed.

Plan:
- Apply override to routing nodes in us-west-2 pool (10:15 PDT)
- Monitor for reduction in 429s and p95 latency
- If fixed, follow up with a permanent quota adjustment after postmortem

Rishi: may need a quick ok on credits/compensation if SLA is materially impacted.

— Dylan
Ops Lead, Serving Runtime

Attachments: config-diff.patch (text)
From: John Lee <john.lee@banked.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@banked.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:30:09-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike -> 429s and latency spike

Monica / team,

Thanks — we’re holding the rollout for 45 minutes as requested. This incident is customer-visible (support tickets are rolling in). Legal and procurement are watching the timeline. Please keep execs informed — Marissa flagged this as potentially needing executive attention if it stretches beyond an hour.

Quick ask: If the temporary override fixes behavior, we will need a documented timeline and proposed permanent settings (burst/quota) so our SREs can approve them. Also need an estimate of user impact (error volume percentage and minutes of degraded response).

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

— John
VP Product, Banked Inc.
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T13:10:42-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production spike -> 429s and latency spike — executive summary + action taken

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding the thread and a short exec summary. Please see the actions taken and the asks from the customer.

Executive summary:
- Incident: Banked traffic ramp triggered repeated token-bucket exhaustion events across three routing workers, causing ~4% 429 rate and p95 latency spike to ~1.8s between 09:04–09:32 PDT.
- Root cause (prelim): account-specific burst window configured at 5s was too small relative to the customer's traffic pattern; enforcement combined with short-window rate limiting caused transient throttling. Not a model-serving capacity issue.
- Actions taken: applied a temporary override (30% bump + burst window -> 20s) to us-west-2 routing pool at 10:15 PDT; observed 429 rate drop to <0.2% and p95 latencies return to baseline within 4 minutes.
- Next steps: follow up with a proposed permanent quota/burst profile, update routing docs, and schedule a postmortem with Banked SREs. Customer asked for: (1) documented timeline, (2) permanent settings recommendation, (3) estimate of user impact.

Risks / exec asks:
- If SLA credits are requested, we will need an approval path for modest credit grants (Rishi).
- Recommend a short PR to the routing policy defaults to add more conservative burst windows for enterprise accounts hitting high short-term ramps. This is a product / policy change that impacts economics — need leadership sign-off.

I’ll draft the customer timeline and permanent config recommendation and share in the runbook link below.

Runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/runbooks/throttle-response.md
PagerDuty: https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-78934

— Monica
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
